guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, init_q is cleared to 0.
When init_q is high and en_i is low, init_q is cleared to 0.
When init_i and en_i are both high, init_q is set to 1.
In all other cases (no reset, not init_q&&!en_i, not init_i&&en_i), init_q retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: External logic must ensure that when init_i is asserted, en_i is also asserted; otherwise init_q will not be set.
assumptions.risk: Missed initialization may leave the key manager in an unconfigured state.

assumptions.claim: External logic must ensure en_i remains asserted throughout the initialization period, because any deassertion of en_i while init_q is high will clear init_q.
assumptions.risk: Premature clearing of init_q could abort initialization, leaving partial or unsafe state.

uncertain_points.claim: The intended behavior of init_q (sticky flag, pulse, or level-sensitive status) is unclear. The clearing on !en_i suggests en_i serves as an active-low clear, but the overall protocol is ambiguous.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect integration with other blocks could lead to unexpected init_q toggling or missed initialization sequences.

uncertain_points.claim: When init_q is high and en_i is high, init_q remains 1 regardless of init_i. If en_i never goes low, init_q stays high permanently, potentially acting as a stuck enable. Is this intended?
uncertain_points.cond: init_q == 1 and en_i == 1 and init_i == 0 (or any init_i)
uncertain_points.risk: A stuck init_q could permanently enable a critical path or mask re-initialization requests.

uncertain_points.claim: The usage of init_q outside this module is not visible; it likely gates other logic. Need to verify that the clearing condition (en_i deassertion) does not violate assumptions of downstream consumers.
uncertain_points.risk: If downstream logic expects init_q to remain set until explicit clear, unexpected deassertion could cause data corruption.
